terms.gloss: the will and power of a god; a deity
evidence: Cic. Div. 1.120: deō, cujus nūminī pārent omnia (Lewis & Short)
Tac. Ann. 1.10: templa et effigiēs nūminum (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Properly a nod of the head, hence a command; then a god’s will and sway, the classical sense; then the god (Lewis & Short).

phrases.latin: dī inmortālēs suō nūmine atque auxiliō sua templa atque urbis tēcta dēfendunt
phrases.english: the immortal gods defend their temples and the houses of the city with their own power and help

sources: Lewis & Short: numen
